question: When hidden witnesses joined by the q-colouring law each have exactly q neighbours, is the relation on the pendant leaves a K1-K3 knot exactly when the witness graph is a Gallai tree?

definitions.witness network: a connected simple graph W on the hidden vertices; vertex v receives q - deg_W(v) pendant leaves (the knot's variables), so every witness has exactly q neighbours
definitions.composite relation: the set of leaf colourings (each leaf a value in 0..q-1) that extend to a proper q-colouring of W plus leaves, i.e. for which W is colourable from the lists L(v) = [q] minus the colours of v's leaves
definitions.Gallai tree: a connected graph every block (maximal 2-connected subgraph, or bridge) of which is a complete graph or an odd cycle
definitions.knot: K1-K3 over finite domains: the relation is a proper subset of the full product, every projection forgetting one leaf is the full product, and it is nonempty
definitions.outside the hypothesis: witness graphs with a vertex of degree above q (no leaves there), recorded as observations only

public_inputs.graphs: every connected simple graph on 1 to 6 vertices up to isomorphism, generated by brute force and reduced by a canonical form
public_inputs.within hypothesis: maximum degree at most q, total leaves at most 9 for q = 3 and at most 7 for q = 4
public_inputs.outside hypothesis: maximum degree exactly q + 1, total leaves within the same caps

forbidden_inputs: the Gallai test is never used to compute a relation

predictions.P1: within the hypothesis, the composite relation passes K1-K3 exactly when W is a Gallai tree
predictions.P2: within the hypothesis, when W is not a Gallai tree, every leaf colouring extends (the relation is full)
predictions.P3: a single complete graph K_q, and for q = 3 every odd cycle, excludes exactly the q all-equal patterns; a single vertex (a star) excludes exactly the patterns using all q colours
predictions.P4: outside the hypothesis, some witness graph (for example two triangles sharing a vertex when q = 3) still gives a knot, so degree exactly q is not necessary

primary_observable: per (q, W): vertices, edges, degrees, leaves, Gallai flag and block types, number of allowed and excluded leaf colourings, K1-K3 verdict, and the type of the excluded patterns
cheapest_meaningful_control: (C1) even cycles C4 and C6 must give no knot; (C2) a Gallai test that wrongly accepts even cycles as blocks must disagree with the computed verdicts somewhere; (C3) check_result.py recomputes every relation with a separate brute-force solver and re-derives Gallai flags with its own block decomposition
independent_check: check_result.py enumerates complete colourings of W instead of searching, uses its own block decomposition and canonical form, and recomputes every verdict and prediction
decision_or_followup_rule: A signal is P1-P3 holding on every census case. Any counterexample within the hypothesis stops ticket B until it is understood. P4 informs the scope of B's theorem.
first_executable_signal: the scan of 2026-10-20 (disposable): star, triangle, C5 and K4 give knots; C4 and C6 give none; two triangles sharing a vertex (degree 4, q = 3) give a knot
stop_rule: Stop after the declared roster or budget; stop early only on a solver or control failure.
nonclaims: Finite enumeration on the declared graphs only; the general statement belongs to ticket B.
Proper colourings with pendant leaves only; no other laws and no claim about witnesses of degree above q beyond the recorded observations.
No claim about native structure, distance or physics.
notes: Feasibility scan on 2026-10-20: q = 3 star 21/27 allowed (knot), triangle with one leaf each excludes exactly the 3 all-equal patterns (knot), C4 and C6 exclude nothing, C5 excludes the 3 all-equal patterns (knot), triangle with a pendant star is a knot, two triangles sharing a vertex give a knot; q = 4 K4 excludes the 4 all-equal patterns, C4 excludes nothing.
